title: Δέλφαξ καὶ πρόβατα
part: The Pig and the Sheep (Chambry 94 · Perry 85)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 94 (= Perry 85). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔν τινι ποίμνῃ προβάτων δέλφαξ εἰσελθὼν ἐνέμετο.
sentences.tr: En tini poimnēi probatōn delphax eiselthōn enemeto.
sentences.l: In a certain flock of sheep a pig, having entered, was feeding.
sentences.i: A pig got in among a flock of sheep and fed there.
sentences.n: ἐν with the dative where English wants 'into': the phrase states where he ended up, and all the movement is carried by εἰσελθών. νέμομαι in the middle is 'to feed oneself, to graze'.

sentences.t: Καὶ δή ποτε τοῦ ποιμένος συλλαμβάνοντος αὐτόν, ἐκεκράγει τε καὶ ἀντέτεινε.
sentences.tr: Kai dē pote tou poimenos syllambanontos auton, ekekragei te kai anteteine.
sentences.l: And so one day, the shepherd seizing him, he was both screaming and straining against him.
sentences.i: And one day, when the shepherd took hold of him, he screamed and struggled.
sentences.n: Genitive absolute in the present, τοῦ ποιμένος συλλαμβάνοντος: the seizing goes on while he screams. ἐκεκράγει is the pluperfect of κράζω, but κέκραγα is a perfect with present force ('I am shouting'), so its pluperfect means simply 'he was shouting'.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ προβάτων αἰτιωμένων αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῷ βοᾶν καὶ λεγόντων· « Ἡμᾶς μὲν συνεχῶς συλλαμβάνει καὶ οὐ κράζομεν, » ἔφη πρὸς ταῦτα· « Ἀλλ᾽ οὐχ ὁμοία γε τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ἡ ἐμὴ σύλληψις· ὑμᾶς γὰρ ἢ διὰ τὰ ἔρια ἀγρεύει ἢ διὰ τὸ γάλα, ἐμὲ δὲ διὰ τὰ κρέα. »
sentences.tr: Tōn de probatōn aitiōmenōn auton epi tōi boan kai legontōn· « Hēmas men synechōs syllambanei kai ou krazomen, » ephē pros tauta· « All’ ouch homoia ge tēi hymeterāi hē emē syllēpsis· hymas gar ē dia ta eria agreuei ē dia to gala, eme de dia ta krea. »
sentences.l: And the sheep accusing him for the shouting and saying: « Us he seizes continually, and we do not scream, » he said in answer to this: « But my seizure, at any rate, is not like yours; for you he hunts either for the wool or for the milk, but me for the meat. »
sentences.i: And when the sheep reproached him for the noise and said: « He takes hold of us all the time, and we do not scream, » he answered: « But being taken means nothing like the same thing for me as for you: he catches you for your wool or your milk, but me for my meat. »
sentences.n: ἐπὶ τῷ βοᾶν is an articular infinitive after ἐπί, 'on the ground of the shouting'. ὁμοία takes a dative of what a thing resembles, τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ — 'like yours'. γε sharpens the denial. The pig's argument is exact: the sheep are harvested and go on living, and he alone is being killed.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι εἰκότως ἐκεῖνοι ἀνοιμώζουσιν οἷς ὁ κίνδυνος οὐ περὶ χρημάτων ἐστίν, ἀλλα περὶ σωτηρίας.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti eikotōs ekeinoi anoimōzousin hois ho kindynos ou peri chrēmatōn estin, alla peri sōtērias.
sentences.l: The story shows that with good reason those wail aloud for whom the danger is not over money but over survival.
sentences.i: The story shows that they have good reason to cry out whose danger is not to their property but to their life.
sentences.n: The relative οἷς is a dative of interest, 'for whom'. σωτηρία is deliverance, keeping one's life — the pig's point exactly. Chambry prints ἀλλα here without its accent; the word is ἀλλά.
